name: Huacachina
tagline: A real palm-fringed oasis surrounded by towering desert dunes, built for dune buggies, sandboarding and watching the sun go down.
highlight: Cresting a towering dune at sunset in a dune buggy, the whole oasis suddenly visible below, a tiny green circle in an ocean of sand.
shortDescription: A small, genuine oasis village surrounded by towering desert dunes, built almost entirely around dune buggy rides, sandboarding and desert sunsets.
metaDescription: A Huacachina travel guide: the oasis, dune buggy rides, sandboarding, food and how to plan a visit to Peru's desert oasis village.
nearestAirport: María Reiche Neuman Airport (NZC), or via Lima and an overland transfer
knownFor: Desert dunes, dune buggy rides, sandboarding
goodFor: Adventure sports, desert scenery, a short detour from Lima

image.file: File:Oasis de Huacachina, Ica, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 19-22 PAN.JPG
image.alt: The palm-fringed oasis of Huacachina surrounded by desert dunes

intro: Huacachina is a real oasis, a small palm-fringed lagoon surrounded by some of the tallest sand dunes in South America, rising more than 100 metres in places right at the village's edge.

It's built almost entirely around one thing — using those dunes for adventure, whether racing across them in a dune buggy or sandboarding down their steep faces as the light turns gold in the late afternoon.
Most visitors treat it as a short, high-energy detour on Peru's southern coast, a night or two between Lima and Nazca that feels unlike anywhere else in the country.

whyVisit.intro: Huacachina's case rests on being a real desert oasis built for adventure, unlike anywhere else on a typical Peru itinerary.

points.title: It's a real, natural oasis
points.text: Not a manufactured tourist attraction, though tourism now sustains the small village around it.

points.title: The dunes are among South America's tallest
points.text: Rising over 100 metres right at the oasis's edge, dramatic at any time of day.

points.title: Dune buggy rides are a real adrenaline rush
points.text: Fast, steep runs across the dunes unlike any other activity in Peru.

points.title: Sandboarding here is accessible to beginners
points.text: Guides and equipment make it approachable even without prior boarding experience.

points.title: It's an easy addition to a coastal Peru itinerary
points.text: A short detour between Lima and Nazca, not requiring a dedicated separate trip.

attractionsIntro: Huacachina's essential sights are all variations on the same striking theme — a green oasis ringed by towering sand.

attractions.name: The Huacachina oasis

image.file: File:Oasis de Huacachina, Ica, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 18.JPG
image.alt: The Huacachina oasis lagoon and surrounding palm trees

attractions.text: A real natural lagoon, its palm-fringed shores forming a striking green circle against the surrounding desert.
attractions.tip: A gentle walk around the lagoon's edge offers the classic oasis view without a dune climb.

attractions.name: The surrounding sand dunes

image.alt: The towering sand dunes surrounding Huacachina

attractions.text: Among the tallest dunes in South America, rising directly from the oasis's edge in every direction.
attractions.tip: The climb up on foot is strenuous — most visitors reach the higher dunes by buggy instead.

attractions.name: The oasis lagoon

image.alt: The lagoon at the centre of the Huacachina oasis

attractions.text: The literal centre of the village, a small lagoon that gives the oasis its name and defining character.
attractions.tip: Reflections on the still water are especially striking in the early morning.

attractions.name: Panoramic dune views

image.file: File:Oasis de Huacachina, Ica, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 19-22 PAN.JPG
image.alt: Panoramic views over the Huacachina dunes

attractions.text: Sweeping views from the higher dunes, the oasis shrinking to a tiny green speck against the vast desert.
attractions.tip: A dune buggy tour typically stops at a high point specifically for this view.

attractions.name: The oasis at dusk

image.file: File:Oasis de Huacachina, Ica, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 23.JPG

attractions.text: One of the best times to see the oasis, warm light catching the palms and the surrounding dunes turning gold.
attractions.tip: Time a dune buggy tour to end around sunset for the best light.

attractions.name: Huacachina's boardwalk

image.file: File:Oasis de Huacachina, Ica, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 24-26 PAN.JPG

attractions.text: A pleasant, easy walk circling the small lagoon, past the village's restaurants and guesthouses.
attractions.tip: The whole loop takes well under an hour, an easy way to get oriented on arrival.

attractions.name: The dunes at sunset

image.file: File:Oasis de Huacachina, Ica, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 27-30 PAN.JPG

attractions.text: The classic end to a Huacachina day, the desert's shifting colours as the sun drops toward the horizon.
attractions.tip: Bring a jacket — desert temperatures drop noticeably once the sun goes down.

thingsToDoIntro: Huacachina exists almost entirely for its dunes, and the classic activities here reward exactly that.

thingsToDo.title: Ride a dune buggy across the sand

image.alt: The dunes surrounding Huacachina, the setting for dune buggy tours

thingsToDo.text: The essential Huacachina experience, a fast, steep-dropping ride across the dunes in a modified open-top buggy.
thingsToDo.tip: Hold on tight — drivers take the steep drops at real speed, and it's a thrilling ride.

thingsToDo.title: Sandboard down the dunes

image.file: File:Oasis de Huacachina, Ica, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 19-22 PAN.JPG
image.alt: The steep dunes above Huacachina used for sandboarding

thingsToDo.text: Accessible even for first-timers, most buggy tours stop partway through for a chance to board down a dune face.
thingsToDo.tip: Lying flat rather than standing is the easier, more common approach for beginners.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the boardwalk around the lagoon

image.file: File:Oasis de Huacachina, Ica, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 24-26 PAN.JPG
image.alt: Walking the boardwalk around Huacachina's lagoon

thingsToDo.text: A relaxed way to spend an hour, taking in the oasis at a slower pace than a buggy tour allows.
thingsToDo.tip: A nice way to start or end a day, away from the dune activities' adrenaline.

thingsToDo.title: Watch sunset over the dunes

image.file: File:Oasis de Huacachina, Ica, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 27-30 PAN.JPG
image.alt: Sunset over the dunes at Huacachina

thingsToDo.text: An essential end to a Huacachina day, watching the desert's colours shift as the sun drops.
thingsToDo.tip: Many buggy tours are specifically timed to end at a high dune for sunset.

thingsToDo.title: Relax at an oasis-side café
thingsToDo.text: A welcome way to recover after a dusty afternoon on the dunes, with several cafés overlooking the lagoon.
thingsToDo.tip: A good spot to rehydrate before or after any dune activity in the heat.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph the oasis from a high dune

image.alt: Photographing the Huacachina oasis from a high dune

thingsToDo.text: A rewarding short climb, or buggy ride, for the classic postcard shot of the oasis surrounded by sand.
thingsToDo.tip: Early morning or late afternoon light gives the most striking contrast between the green oasis and gold dunes.

foodIntro: Huacachina's food benefits from the wider Ica region's reputation for pisco and desert-valley wine.

foods.name: Pisco

image.alt: A pisco sour made with Peru's national spirit

foods.text: Produced throughout the surrounding Ica valley, among Peru's finest pisco-growing land.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and bars throughout the oasis.

foods.name: Ica valley wine
foods.text: A lesser-known but worthwhile Peruvian product, made in the same desert valleys as the region's famous pisco.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants throughout Huacachina and nearby Ica.

foods.name: Ceviche

image.alt: Ceviche, Peru's national dish of citrus-cured raw fish

foods.text: Available given the oasis's proximity to the coast, a refreshing option in the desert heat.

foods.name: Lomo saltado

image.alt: Lomo saltado, a Peruvian stir-fry of beef, onions and fries

foods.text: A reliable classic, found on menus throughout the small oasis village.

foods.name: Tequeños
foods.text: A beloved Peruvian bar snack, crispy fried pastry rolls filled with cheese, popular alongside a pisco sour.
foods.whereToTry: Bars and restaurants throughout the oasis.

foods.name: Chicha morada
foods.text: A refreshing non-alcoholic purple corn drink, well suited to the desert heat.

areas.name: Around the lagoon
areas.bestFor: Being central to every restaurant and tour operator
areas.text: The village is small enough that nearly every guesthouse sits within a few minutes' walk of the water.

areas.name: Ica town

gettingThere.intro: Huacachina is reached by road, a short detour from the nearby city of Ica on Peru's southern coastal route.

options.text: A comfortable journey of around four to five hours to Ica, plus a short taxi to Huacachina.
options.detail: Regular daily departures run on Peru's southern coastal bus route.

options.mode: Bus or shared van from Nazca
options.text: A short hop, around an hour and a half.
options.detail: A natural pairing given the two destinations' proximity.

options.mode: Private transfer or tour from Lima
options.text: A convenient option, often combined with a Paracas or Nazca stop.
options.detail: A popular way to see several southern coast highlights in one trip.

gettingAround.intro: Huacachina is tiny and entirely walkable, with dune activities arranged directly through your accommodation.

options.text: Covers the whole oasis easily — it's a very small village.
options.detail: The full boardwalk loop around the lagoon takes well under an hour.

options.text: The way to reach the higher dunes and any sandboarding spots.
options.detail: Widely available and easy to book directly through your hotel.

bestTime.headline: April to December for the mildest desert temperatures
bestTime.summary: Huacachina's desert climate stays warm year-round, with summer months bringing more intense midday heat.

seasons.text: Mild, comfortable temperatures for dune activities without the peak summer heat.
Still mild with thinner crowds than peak summer.
Hot at midday, though still workable with an early or late dune buggy tour.

bestTime.avoid: A midday dune buggy tour in peak summer — far more comfortable timed for morning or late afternoon.

itinerary.title: One day in Huacachina
itinerary.intro: A single, well-paced day built around a dune buggy and sandboarding tour timed for sunset.

days.title: The dunes
days.summary: The oasis boardwalk and a dune buggy and sandboarding tour.
days.morning: Walk the boardwalk around the lagoon.
days.afternoon: Relax at an oasis-side café out of the midday heat.
days.evening: A dune buggy and sandboarding tour timed for sunset.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Huacachina visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book a sunset-timed dune buggy tour for the best light and cooler temperatures.
Wear sunglasses and cover your face — sand kicks up significantly during buggy rides.
Bring a jacket for after dark — desert temperatures drop sharply once the sun sets.
Pack a change of clothes — sandboarding and buggy rides get sandy.
Stay hydrated throughout the day, given the desert heat.
Combine Huacachina with Nazca given the short distance between the two.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Huacachina?
faq.a: One day covers the oasis and a dune buggy and sandboarding tour comfortably; an overnight allows a more relaxed pace.
Yes — it's a real natural lagoon, though tourism now sustains the small village that has grown up around it.
Yes — most tours include basic instruction, and lying flat rather than standing is a common, easier approach.
Its palm-fringed oasis surrounded by towering sand dunes, and the dune buggy and sandboarding activities built around them.

faq.q: Can you visit Huacachina as a day trip from Lima?
faq.a: It's possible but rushed, given the four to five hour drive each way — an overnight stay is more comfortable.
Generally yes, with sensible precautions during dune buggy rides — always use the provided seatbelts and follow your driver's instructions.
